data.name: Hermann
data.gender_notes: Hermann is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Germanic root ‘herm’ meaning an army or a soldier. The name can also be derived from the name Hermes, the Greek god of trade, commerce, and thieves. The name Hermann carries the meaning “Soldier, Arnold” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Hermann usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier, arnold and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hermann belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier, Arnold.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hermann total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: הרמן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הרמן הוא שם פרטי שמקורו בארמית, ומשמעותו היא ארמי חזק, גיבור או לוחם. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'ארם' שפירושה ארם, ו'מן' שפירושה איש או גבר. השם הרמן מופיע בתנך כהתייחסות לאנשים שונים, ביניהם הרמן איש אדמון, שהיה אחד מהאבות של עם ישראל.

in_greek.name: Χέρμαν
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χέρμαν προέρχεται από τη γερμανική λέξη 'Hermann', που σημαίνει 'άνθρωπος από τη Γερμανία' ή 'Γερμανός'. Στην αρχαία Ελλάδα, το όνομα Χέρμαν δεν ήταν συνηθισμένο, αλλά με την έλευση των Γερμανικών φύλων στην Ευρώπη, το όνομα Χέρμαν άρχισε να χρησιμοποιείται ευρέως.

in_latin.name: Hermannus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hermannus originem habet in lingua Germanica, significans hominem Germanum vel virum robustum. In Ecclesia primitiva, nomen Hermannus fuit usitatum inter fideles, qui virtutem et robur in Deo quaesiverunt.

in_english.name: Hermann
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hermann originates from the Germanic words 'heri' meaning army and 'man' meaning man. It signifies a Germanic warrior or a man from Germany. Historically, the name Hermann was popularized by Saint Hermann of Cologne, a 13th-century German saint. The name symbolizes strength, courage, and loyalty, reflecting the values of the early Christian church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hermann was widely adopted among the Germanic peoples, especially in the Middle Ages, as a strong and masculine name for warriors and leaders. Market towns and even cities such as Hermannstadt (now Sibiu, Romania) were named after this moniker, evoking the bravery and might associated with this name.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Hermann can be found in its potential connection to the Greek god Hermes. As the god of commerce, Hermes is associated with the Christian virtues of faith, hope, and charity. In the context of a Christian name, Hermann could be seen as a reminder to be a faithful warrior in the service of God, working tirelessly to bring not only material wealth but also spiritual growth to oneself and to others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Hermann: Der Mann des Heiligen Hermes, den Gott beschützt (The man of the Holy Hermes, whom God protects) or Der Mann des Geistessymbole Hermes (The man of the spiritual symbol Hermes), symbolizing wisdom, guidance, and divine protection.
